In 2015 I think that most people should be satisfied with a GNU+Linux operating system. Sure, there's always someone who needs (or think he needs) a very specific program, but most people really just surf the web and play Facebook games.

I've been using GNU+Linux distribution for 7 years now, I've used Mandriva, Ubuntu, Arch and now OpenSuse. I think OpenSuse is a really nice choice because it has a lot of tools that makes life easier (especially if you're coming from Windows) and it really works well (upgrades between different versions have been a breeze; I cannot say the same for Ubuntu unfortunately).

So, unless you absolutely, really need a very specific program for which there is no alternative, you can safely switch. The entry cost really pays for itself in the end.

The rules: We all awake in the dirt with ONLY our clothes and the blueprints of the Impala with a note instructing us to build it from scratch and life as we know it will be restored. We have no buildings or infrastructure, no food, no tools or machines, no books or communication tools. Just our bare hands, our collective knowledge/skills (our memories are all intact) and the full schematics of the Impala. The one we build must be a replica that a car buff who owns an Impala would be unable to discern from his own car, so even the radio must work although it wouldn't pick up any stations. Once we do this, life as we know it will magically be restored.
How long would it take humanity to build a 95 Impala from scratch if we all fell asleep and woke up in the stone age?

Keep in mind we would still have to feed and shelter ourselves. Then we must find a way to bring the right minds and materials together in one place. That alone will take quite an effort, but needless to say all of humanity save for a few doomsdayers will be united in this cause. After we get the right minds together, then we need to reinvent the measurement systems and tools needed to fabricate the vehicle, and we of course will need to make the machines that do things like stretching copper into a wire (after we mine it). Beyond that, we will need to create precision machines to print circuit boards and program computers to run those machines.

Personally, I think it would take humanity almost a decade just to make an Impala from scratch... a car that we can produce dozens of in a single day right now. Mindboggling how reliant our future is upon our past innovations, isn't it?

Well, The first thing that is going to happen is that most of humanity will die of starvation within a few weeks. Stone age earth just can't deal with that many people.

Then, since there is no efficient way to transfer knowledge, most of what is known is lost as people die.

Now we are left with a few thousand very frustrated humans whose knowledge and skills don't apply due to lack of tools.

In the end, the Impala blueprints starts a very weird religion, and the first one is built in 1844 when the infrastructure is available and this causes a global war between the haves and have-nots.

I think we'd still number in the hundreds of millions after a few weeks, though I shudder to think that the majority remaining have probably subsisted on the flesh of those who died. Hopefully those who are aware that they possess rare or critical knowledge will endeavor to record it if they sense they won't be around to share it much longer.

Communication will be hugely important of course, so it stands to reason that we will at least have to stretch a telegraph across the continent if not the ocean. I suppose GM would try to gather its personnel in short order, though that may be difficult with respect to engineers they contract with overseas for certain parts.

A jaw-dropping variety of workers, from miners to haulers to chemists to smiths to engineers to fabricators to programmers to machines, and that's not even counting the fact that we have to reinvent simple weights and measures. All those are needed just to make a fucking WHEEL on the Impala.

The biggest priority will be getting agriculture and drinking water happening again. It's hard to imagine how many people will be left by the time we've stopped dying of starvation.

We might just fuck things up unrecoverably. For instance, I imagine people will kill and eat every single ancestral cow before anyone manages to set up a breeding program. Seven billion hungry humans are going to hunt pretty much everything edible to extinction pretty fast, at least on land.
